problemStatement.formal: Let $c>0$ and $n$ be some large integer. What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of a subset of $A$? Does this depend on $n$ in an irregular way?
problemStatement.plain: Let $c>0$ and $n$ be some large integer. What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of a subset of $A$? Does this depend on $n$ in an irregular way?

proven: Empty set is non-representing for n > 0
Non-representing is monotone under subset inclusion
Full range is optimal when sum < n
open: Asymptotic growth rate of maxNonReprSize (conjectured Theta(sqrt(n)))
